answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a full winter season staffing a real tundra research outpost. The outpost is supplied by a single ocean voyage per season, and each resident repairs the station's gear at its own forge bench, with the work logged and spot-checked live. One person cannot winter at two outposts at once, so every extra fake identity costs another human's whole winter, another berth on the supply ship, another forge slot, and an outside-money fee that doubles per identity on the same funding trail.
